note.summary: Section 684 ITEPA 2003 empowers the Commissioners for HMRC to make PAYE regulations covering assessment, charge, collection and recovery of income tax on PAYE income, and sets out an extensive list of matters those regulations may cover, including deductions/repayments via tax tables, coding out of self-assessment underpayments and certain charges (e.g. high income child benefit charge, winter fuel payment charge), recovery of relevant debts via PAYE coding, information requirements on employers and payment service providers, interest on late-paid or overpaid sums, security requirements, appeals, and offences for failure to give security. It caps non-consensual coding-out deductions at £17,000 per tax year (subject to Treasury amendment) and confirms PAYE regulations override other Income Tax Acts provisions and preserve tribunal appeal rights. This section is primarily about PAYE machinery for employers/payers rather than the SA return itself, but is directly relevant to SA because coding-out (item 2, 2A) interacts with self-assessment underpayments and debts.

note.summary: This chunk sets out PAYE rules (sections 690A-690C ITEPA 2003) for employers of internationally mobile employees from tax year 2025-26 onwards. Section 690A allows an employer (or designated 'appropriate person') to notify HMRC of the estimated non-PAYE proportion of mobile payments so that portion is not treated as PAYE income; the notice must be acknowledged by HMRC to have effect and can be superseded or cease to apply in specified circumstances. Section 690B allows HMRC officers to issue a direction determining the non-PAYE proportion or requiring full PAYE treatment, which takes effect on giving and can be varied with at least 30 days' notice. Section 690C provides transitional rules for employees who were internationally mobile, non-resident, or split-year/remittance-basis claimants in tax years before 2025-26, requiring employers to estimate the PAYE-taxable proportion of general earnings payments.
